subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Nicodemus’ encounter with Jesus Christ
overview: John 3:1-5 tells how Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council, came to Jesus at night. Jesus told him that no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again, of water and the Spirit. In this sub-strand you will retell that meeting, learn about repentance and baptism, and recite John 3:16.

lessons.title: Nicodemus comes to Jesus at night
objectives: Explain what Jesus meant by being born again in this passage.
lessons.intro: Some people come to Jesus with questions they do not want a crowd to hear. Nicodemus came at night. Jesus answered him with a truth about a new beginning.
lessons.notes:
Read John 3:1-5 and retell only that conversation.

Nicodemus was a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council. He came to Jesus at night and said, "Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher who has come from God. For no one could perform the signs you are doing if God were not with him."

Jesus replied, "Very truly I tell you, no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again."

Nicodemus asked, "How can someone be born when they are old? Surely they cannot enter a second time into their mother's womb to be born!"

Jesus answered, "Very truly I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God unless they are born of water and the Spirit."

### What the words mean
A Pharisee was a Jewish teacher who was careful about the law. The ruling council was the group of leaders. Rabbi means teacher. Signs are the mighty works Jesus was doing, which showed Nicodemus that God was with Him.

Born again does not mean a second birth from a mother, which is what Nicodemus thought. Jesus corrected him. It means a new life from God. Verse 5 says this new birth is of water and the Spirit. Without it, a person cannot see or enter the kingdom of God.

The passage shows Nicodemus respectful and puzzled. He already called Jesus a teacher come from God. Jesus told him he needed more than respect. He needed to be born again. Do not add later scenes that these verses do not contain. Role-play the night visit, the praise, the saying about being born again, Nicodemus' question, and Jesus' answer about water and the Spirit.

keyWords.meaning: a Jewish teacher careful about God's law; Nicodemus was one
the new life from God that Jesus said a person needs in order to see the kingdom
the mighty works of Jesus that showed God was with Him

activity.title: Role-play the night conversation
steps: Role-play Nicodemus' encounter with Jesus: the night visit, the words about signs, and the teaching about being born again.
Say how a person can respond to Christ's saving grace: by listening, repenting and believing.
If a video on Nicodemus is available, watch it and check which parts match John 3:1-5.

practice.question: Who was Nicodemus, and when did he come to Jesus?
practice.answer: He was a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council. He came at night.

practice.question: What did he say about Jesus?
practice.answer: He called Him Rabbi and said Jesus was a teacher come from God, because no one could do those signs unless God was with Him.

practice.question: What did Jesus say a person must be, to see and enter the kingdom of God?
practice.answer: Born again, of water and the Spirit.

summary: Nicodemus came to Jesus at night and said God was with Him.
Jesus said no one can see the kingdom unless they are born again.
That new birth is of water and the Spirit, not a return to a mother's womb.

lessons.title: Repentance draws us close to Christ
objectives: Explain how repentance of sins draws a person close to Christ.
Say how he or she will respond to Christ's saving grace.
lessons.intro: Nicodemus was an important teacher, but Jesus still spoke to him about a new birth. Being close to Christ is not a matter of a high position. It begins when a person turns from sin.
lessons.notes:
Repentance means turning away from sin and turning to God. Jesus told Nicodemus that entry into the kingdom needs a new birth. A person who loves sin and will not turn is not drawing near. A person who repents is answering the call to be born again.

### How repentance draws us close
- We admit that we have done wrong. Pride keeps us far away.
- We ask Jesus for forgiveness.
- We stop the wrong action: lying, stealing, cruelty, impure talk.
- We start the right action: truth, kindness, prayer, obedience.
- We come to Him even if, like Nicodemus, we still have questions. He receives people who come honestly.

Saving grace is the kindness of Christ that saves people who do not deserve it. Nicodemus had learnt that the signs showed God was with Jesus. Responding to that grace means more than noticing the signs. It means trusting Jesus and turning from sin.

Discuss this in a group. One learner may say, "I will stop cheating and ask God to forgive me." Another may say, "I will pray every night and obey my parents." Those are real responses. Humility belongs here. Nicodemus, a leader, still had to be taught. Role-play him listening, not arguing to win. Respect is shown when we let Jesus' words correct us.

You can be young and still repent. Age was Nicodemus' puzzle, not a barrier Jesus accepted. "How can someone be born when they are old?" Jesus answered with God's work: water and the Spirit. Whether a person is old or in Grade 4, the way near to Christ is repentance and trust.

keyWords.meaning: turning away from sin and turning to God
God's kindness that saves, which we do not earn
a modest heart that is willing to be taught

activity.title: Discuss repentance
steps: Discuss how repentance of sins can draw you to Christ.
Each learner says one way he or she will respond to Christ's saving grace.
Role-play Nicodemus listening humbly to Jesus.
Write a one-sentence prayer of repentance.

practice.question: What is repentance?
practice.answer: Turning away from sin and turning to God.

practice.question: Why was Nicodemus' high position not enough?
practice.answer: Jesus said no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again.

practice.question: Give two ways to respond to Christ's saving grace.
practice.answer: Any two: admit sin, ask for forgiveness, stop a wrong action, obey, pray, believe in Jesus.

summary: Repentance turns a person from sin to Christ.
A high position cannot replace the new birth.
We respond to Christ's grace by believing, repenting and obeying.

lessons.title: Baptism and John 3:16
objectives: Discuss the importance of baptism to Christians today.
Recite John 3:16 and say what it means to believe in Jesus.
lessons.intro: Jesus told Nicodemus that the new birth is of water and the Spirit. Christians connect this teaching with baptism and with faith. John 3:16 tells why believing in Jesus matters.
lessons.notes:
### Baptism
Baptism is the Christian act of being baptised with water in the name of Jesus. In John 3:5 Jesus says no one can enter the kingdom of God unless they are born of water and the Spirit. Christians today take baptism seriously because Jesus joined water and the Spirit with entering the kingdom.

Baptism is important because:

- Jesus taught that the new birth involves water and the Spirit.
- It shows that a person has turned from sin and belongs to Jesus.
- It is a beginning of a new life, which is what "born again" means.
- The church obeys this teaching and welcomes the baptised person.
- It is done in public, so the believer is not hiding faith.

Baptism is not a magic wash that leaves the heart unchanged. It belongs with repentance and belief. A learner prepares by listening to the Bible, talking with parents and church leaders, and turning from sin. Different churches baptise at different ages. Speak respectfully about the practice of your church, and remember the verse that unites Christians: new birth by water and the Spirit.

### John 3:16
Recite: "For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life."

God loved the world. He gave His Son. Whoever believes in Jesus will not perish but will have eternal life. Eternal life is life with God that death does not end. Believing means trusting Jesus, not merely knowing His name.

Tell how you respond to this verse: thank God for His love, believe in Jesus, repent, and follow Him. Sing a song about Nicodemus' meeting with Jesus and about God's love in John 3:16.

keyWords.meaning: the Christian act of being baptised with water, joined in John 3:5 with the new birth
to trust Jesus, not only to know His name
life with God that John 3:16 promises to whoever believes in Jesus

activity.title: Recite John 3:16
steps: Say why baptism is important to Christians today, using John 3:5.
Write John 3:16 on a flash card and recite it.
Each learner tells how he or she responds to John 3:16.
Sing a song on Nicodemus' encounter with Jesus and on God's love.

practice.question: What does John 3:5 say is needed to enter the kingdom of God?
practice.answer: To be born of water and the Spirit.

practice.question: Give two reasons why baptism is important to Christians.
practice.answer: Any two: Jesus taught new birth of water and the Spirit; it shows we belong to Jesus; it marks a new life; it follows repentance and belief.

practice.question: Recite John 3:16.
practice.answer: For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life.

summary: Jesus said people must be born of water and the Spirit.
Baptism is important because it belongs with that new birth, repentance and faith.
John 3:16: God loved the world and gave His Son so that believers may have eternal life.

quiz.question: Nicodemus' conversation in this sub-strand is in:
Nicodemus was...
options: a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council

quiz.question: He came to Jesus...
options: at noon in the market only
during the feeding of a crowd, in this passage
quiz.explanation: John 3:2 says he came at night.

quiz.question: Nicodemus said Jesus was a teacher come from God because:
options: he had read Genesis that morning
quiz.explanation: John 3:2 says no one could do those signs unless God was with Him.

quiz.question: Jesus said no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are:
options: able to enter the womb a second time
quiz.explanation: John 3:3 says they must be born again.

quiz.question: Born of water and the Spirit means, in Jesus' answer:
quiz.answer: The new birth God gives, which Nicodemus could not get by entering his mother's womb again.
quiz.explanation: John 3:4-5 corrects Nicodemus' idea of a physical second birth.

quiz.question: Repentance draws a person close to Christ because:
options: turning from sin is how we answer His call to a new life
leaders do not need to repent
quiz.explanation: Jesus required a new birth, so repentance and trust are the way near to Him.

quiz.question: Baptism is important to Christians today because:
options: Jesus said people must be born of water and the Spirit
quiz.explanation: John 3:5 joins water and the Spirit with entering the kingdom.

quiz.question: John 3:16 says God loved the world and gave:
quiz.explanation: The verse says God gave His one and only Son.

quiz.question: Whoever believes in Jesus will...
quiz.answer: Not perish but have eternal life.
quiz.explanation: That is the promise of John 3:16.
